aprocitentan.label: us3/aprocitentan.json

rows.dose: Usual dose; monitor for oedema/fluid retention

ev: TRYVIO is not recommended in patients with kidney failure (eGFR <15 mL/min) or on dialysis
Patients with renal impairment are at increased risk of edema/fluid retention
Initiation of TRYVIO may cause an initial small decrease in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) that occurs within the first 6 weeks of starting therapy and then stabilizes
TRYVIO is not recommended in patients with kidney failure (eGFR <15 mL/min) or on dialysis
Dialysis is unlikely to be effective because aprocitentan is highly protein-bound

proteinBinding.ev: Aprocitentan is >99% bound to plasma proteins, primarily albumin

ihd.value: Unlikely to be removed by dialysis (label)

aprocitentan.summary: Not recommended at eGFR <15 or on dialysis. CKD raises oedema/fluid-retention risk; small early eGFR dip.

tables.indication: Heart failure / CV risk · US label

ev: Efficacy and safety studies with INPEFA did not enroll patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1
Initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors, including INPEFA, causes a small increase in serum creatinine and decrease in eGFR
Assess renal function prior to initiation of INPEFA and then as clinically indicated

halfLife.ev: Following administration of 200 mg and 400 mg, mean terminal half-life (T1/2) ranged from 21 to 35 hours for sotagliflozin and from 19 to 26 hours for sotagliflozin 3-O-glucuronide

sotagliflozin.summary: Studied down to eGFR 25; not studied below 25 or on dialysis. Early creatinine rise expected.

imlifidase.label: uk3/imlifidase.json

ckd.notes: Patients are on dialysis awaiting transplant; no renal dose statement.
ev: Idefirix is indicated for desensitisation treatment of highly sensitised adult kidney transplant patients with positive crossmatch against an available deceased donor

Antibody-based medicinal products cleaved by imlifidase include, but are not limited to basiliximab, rituximab, alemtuzumab, adalimumab, denosumab, belatacept, etanercept, rabbit anti-thymocyte globulin (rATG) and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg)
Imlifidase does not degrade equine anti-thymocyte globulin and no time interval between administrations needs to be considered

imlifidase.summary: Used before deceased-donor kidney transplant in highly sensitised patients. Cleaves IgG: antibody medicines (basiliximab, rituximab, rATG, IVIG, belatacept) given around it are inactivated.
imlifidase.considerations: EU authorisation (EMA); not approved in the US. Time antibody-based induction and rescue medicines around the imlifidase dose as the SmPC specifies.

vaccine-hepatitis-b-engerix.label: us3/vaccine-hepatitis-b-engerix.json

ev: Adults on Hemodialysis Primary immunization consists of a series of 4 doses (2 mL each) given as a single 2 mL dose or two 1 mL doses on a 0‑, 1‑, 2‑, and 6‑month schedule

rows.dose: Annual anti-HBs; 2 mL booster when below 10 mIU/mL

ev: Adults on Hemodialysis Primary immunization consists of a series of 4 doses (2 mL each) given as a single 2 mL dose or two 1 mL doses on a 0‑, 1‑, 2‑, and 6‑month schedule
Therefore, the need for booster doses should be assessed by annual antibody testing
A 2 mL booster dose (as a single 2 mL dose or two 1 mL doses) should be given when antibody levels decline below 10 mIU/mL1
In hemodialysis patients, antibody response is lower than in healthy persons and protection may persist only as long as antibody levels remain above 10 mIU/mL

vaccine-hepatitis-b-engerix.summary: Adults on haemodialysis: 4 doses of 2 mL (40 mcg) at 0, 1, 2 and 6 months; annual anti-HBs; booster when <10 mIU/mL.
vaccine-hepatitis-b-engerix.considerations: Vaccines are not renally dose-adjusted except where the label gives a dialysis schedule. CDC: hepatitis B vaccination is recommended for all susceptible chronic haemodialysis patients and for people with CKD before they need dialysis; the adult immunization schedule by medical condition has a column for kidney failure, end-stage renal disease or dialysis. Live vaccines can cause adverse reactions with altered immunocompetence (chronic renal disease can itself alter immunocompetence); after transplant, immunosuppression generally rules out live vaccines, so vaccinate before transplant where possible (CDC General Best Practice Guidelines).
